records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — No pagination-boundary test covers a member count exactly divisible by the limit, so the phantom empty final page remains unguarded.
records.rationale: The diff's totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 (admin-group.js.es6), which yields a phantom final page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit; the `next` action would advance offset to user_count and fetch an empty members list while showingLast (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) incorrectly reports it as the last page. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff, though the finding is framed around missing test coverage of that boundary.
records.stripped_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — No pagination-boundary test covers a member count exactly divisible by the limit, so the phantom empty final page remains unguarded.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — Editing a group name before adding or removing members makes the successful mutation refresh an unsaved name, failing the reload or showing another group's members.
records.rationale: The diff shows removeMember/addMembers call self.findMembers() after mutation, and findMembers issues Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json'). If the user has edited the name field in the template ({{text-field value=name}}) without saving, findMembers will fetch members of a nonexistent/other group. Mechanism is verifiable in the diff; severity is an edge case.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Starting member loading from setupController without returning or handling the promise bypasses route error handling, so failed requests leave the member page empty or stale with an unhandled rejection.
records.rationale: The diff replaces the previous pattern in group-members.js.es6 (afterModel returning model.findMembers().then(...)) with setupController calling model.findMembers() without returning the promise. So failed member fetches no longer flow through the route's promise/error handling, and the unreturned rejection can leave the member list empty/stale. The mechanism is accurately described and verifiable from the diff, though the practical severity is modest.
